senses.sense_definition: A manual tool with sliding beads or counters used for performing arithmetic calculations.

examples.text: Merchants in some countries still use an <w>abacus</w> for adding up large numbers quickly.
Children learn basic math by sliding beads on an <w>abacus</w> to visualize addition and subtraction.

senses.sense_definition: The flat slab forming the top part of a column capital.

examples.text: The architect carefully restored the decorative <w>abacus</w> resting atop the ancient stone column.
The square <w>abacus</w> provides a stable base for the architrave above the capital.

senses.sense_definition: A table or tray covered with sand used for drawing geometric figures or performing calculations.

examples.text: Ancient scholars used a sand-covered <w>abacus</w> to trace complex geometric proofs.
Before paper was common, a simple <w>abacus</w> tray served as a workspace for mathematicians.

traits.comment: Refers to historical methods of calculation.

senses.sense_definition: A sideboard, cupboard, or table used for displaying dishes or valuables.

examples.text: The wealthy Roman displayed his gold plates on an ornate <w>abacus</w> in the dining hall.
Archaeologists discovered a marble <w>abacus</w> used for holding cups in the ruins of the villa.
